title: attn-probe-fusion-microkernel: introduce probe-fusion kernel with rope-handshake prefetch
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves attention kernel latency and KV-cache warmup for medium-length sequences (16-512), ~18-28% tail latency reduction for mixed RT workloads. No API changes. Refer rollout notes for canary strategy.
description:
Motivation: Live inference workloads at Redwood show suboptimal tail latency for mixed interactive and streaming traffic where short-chat prefixes are common but occasional long completions occur. Existing fused kernels are tuned for either very short or very long windows; the 'probe-fusion' microkernel introduced here targets the mid-range (seq_len 16-512) where a light-weight probe + rope-handshake prefetcher can significantly reduce first-token latency and smooth KV warming costs.

What this PR does: single continuous change that introduces a new attn-probe microkernel plus scheduler hints and a KV snapshotting shim: (1) attn/probe_fusion.{cu,h}: compact fused QK / rotary-probe path that probes lane occupancy before launching GEMM, reducing wasted warps on sparse rotary offsets; (2) runtime/scheduler: add RouteHint::ProbePreferred and a lightweight async prefetch worker that issues rope-handshake hints to the device for upcoming rotary offsets; (3) kv/cache: KV snapshotting and quick-commit path so probe-prefetch can pre-populate small hot KV slabs without triggering full eviction heuristics; (4) tests/bench: new bench targets and microbench harness to validate latency distribution across mixed batches.

Technical notes: The probe-fusion kernel implements a two-stage flow: small vectorized probe that inspects rotary offset alignment and active head occupancy, followed by a conditional fused QK path that either runs a packed QK+softmax GEMM for densely-aligned lanes or falls back to the standard interleaved QKV kernel for misaligned/fragmented cases. The rope-handshake prefetch is a non-blocking enqueue that sigils upcoming rotary rotation maps so the device can remap threads to contiguous memory ranges for better coalescing. KV snapshotting keeps a 4-way MRU slab for hot prefixes to avoid repeated allocation churn when probe triggers warmups.

Benchmarks: Microbench on c6g/gpu-rt instances; median improvements for representative workloads:
- Chat small (avg seq 40): 20% median latency, 28% 99th latency
- Streaming mixed (prefix 24, tail variable): 12% median, 18% 95th
- Long-only (seq 1024): neutral (-1% to +2%), measured to ensure no regressions
Cost: small increase in kernel variants (~120KB of binary), runtime memory overhead for KV snapshot ~2-6MB per model shard.

Compatibility and rollout: Default is gated behind a runtime config flag 'probe_fusion.enabled=false' in main; rollout plan: enable in Dedicated canaries, then 5% Hosted traffic for models with median seq in target range, monitor latency and errors for 72h, then expand. No public API surface changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests
- [x] Scheduler hooks and backpressure handling
- [x] KV snapshot shim and eviction safety checks
- [x] Microbench and system-level benchmarks
- [x] Docs stub and feature flagging

Related: builds on RFC from ENG-3265 (probe-based scheduling) and pairs with ENG-3301 (kv-snapshotting). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3265/probe-fusion-design (internal).

Risks and mitigations: The primary risk is increased kernel complexity leading to subtle misalignments on older GPU drivers; mitigations: runtime feature gate, explicit driver version check in the runtime that refuses to enable probe_fusion on known-bad drivers, and a conservative default fallback to the standard fused path.

Rollout notes: Use canary config profile 'probe-fusion-canary' in Dedicated and Hosted. Observability: new metrics attn_probe_hits, attn_probe_misses, rope_handshake_latency, kv_snapshot_hot_rate. Alert thresholds included in observability-pack PR (linked).

review_comments:
Linnea: Great design, can we add a safety timeout on the prefetcher queue to avoid unbounded growth?
Author (Aisha): Added a timeout and metric 'prefetch_queue_drop' in second commit.
Devon: Bench results look promising; did you verify driver compatibility on older 11.x stacks?
Author: Yes - runtime will refuse to enable probe_fusion on CUDA<11.8 and driver versions with known warp-atomic bugs.
Rajesh: KV snapshotting looks risky for multi-model hosts, please add per-model memory caps.
Author: Added caps and eviction hooks; default cap is 8MB per shard.
QA: Found flaky failure in probe_fusion_bench on small GPUs; fixed race in prefetcher where worker could access freed shard during shutdown.
Approvals: Linnea approved, Devon approved after driver checks, Rajesh approved after caps. Merge method: squash and merge.
ci_summary: Initial CI: linux-build (pass), cuda-build (fail: flaky timing test), unit-tests (pass), bench-smoke (fail on AMI with older driver). Reran with pinned test timeouts and driver check: all green. Final status: pass.
merge_outcome: squash and merge to main. PR merged by Aisha Patel after approvals and green CI.
notes_for_release: Feature gated; enable in production via runtime flag. Observe metrics attn_probe_hits/misses and kv_snapshot_hot_rate. If probes show high miss rate (>60%) revert via probe_fusion.enabled=false. See rollout playbook in docs/feature_flags.md.
qa_steps: 1) Enable probe_fusion in dedicated canary pool. 2) Run representative traffic for 72h, collect latency histograms and attn_probe metrics. 3) Verify no increase in OOMs, confirm kv_snapshot memory usage under per-shard cap. 4) If regressions observed, flip feature flag and collect traces for root cause.
